fresh_validated_observations.topic: H.R. 5334 creates an observable pre-implementation policy signal before secondary tariffs can take effect
fresh_validated_observations.label: PRIMARY-SOURCE POLICY MECHANISM / PRE-MOVE TIMING REFINEMENT
observed_facts: The enrolled text of H.R. 5334 requires the President, within 30 days after enactment, to raise duties on Russian goods including energy to a rate of up to 500% ad valorem.

Section 113 requires, within 30 days, duties of up to 100% on goods from a qualifying country that knowingly makes new purchases of Russian crude oil or natural gas on or after day 30 and is among the five largest importers over the relevant lookback, or is among the five largest sanctions-evasion facilitators.
The statute permits rate adjustment above zero and up to 100%, contains a natural-gas exception under specified conditions, and requires periodic redetermination of qualifying countries.

Section 113(g) requires the President or USTR to submit a written justification to specified congressional committees at least 10 days before imposing or modifying a Section 113 tariff, including the substantive rationale and methodology.
Section 115 authorizes national-interest waivers subject to certification and congressional reporting. Therefore the enacted statutory ceiling is not the same as a predetermined realized tariff rate.
fresh_validated_observations.inference: The market-relevant process is staged: enactment -> country/purchase qualification -> policy-rate selection -> mandatory advance report -> tariff implementation -> possible waiver/modification. The 10-day advance-report requirement creates a cleaner public timestamp for pre-move causal studies than treating Sep. 18 enactment as if the final tariff were already known and effective.
fresh_validated_observations.pre_move_research_rule: For this law, freeze information at each statutory stage. Capture the first public congressional/USTR justification, selected rate, affected-country determination and waiver state before studying subsequent oil, freight, FX, rates and equity responses. Do not backfill the final tariff into the enactment-day information set.
fresh_validated_observations.capital_flow_chain: secondary-tariff threat -> exposed importer compares U.S. market access with Russian-energy discount -> possible sourcing shift -> substitution demand for non-Russian crude/LNG plus freight/insurance -> physical differentials and inflation expectations -> yields/FX/current-account effects -> cross-asset repricing; waiver or low selected tariff can interrupt the chain before physical flows change.
fresh_validated_observations.decision_support: Crude remains WAIT. The law raises energy/rates tail risk but does not justify a weekend directional oil forecast before implementation details, physical-flow changes and open-market price confirmation.

negative_findings: Do not interpret H.R. 5334's maximum authorized rates as already-realized tariffs.
Do not use Sep. 18 enactment as the sole information timestamp when the statute itself creates later qualification, advance-report, implementation and waiver stages.
Do not infer a weekend crude move from an unverified Riyadh security event.
Do not promote BTC to BUY from weekend price retention alone while the U.S. ETF channel is closed and funding remains elevated versus the two-week baseline.
Do not attribute ZEC's entire move to the wrapper when privacy peers are also strong and wrapper inventory changes can include legacy, in-kind, related-party and corporate-action effects.
